newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Analysts mixed on Indosat 9-mth result.
newsitem.headline: Analysts mixed on Indosat 9-mth result.

text.p: A 5.5 percent rise in net profits announced by PT Indonesian Satellite Corporation Tbk (PT Indosat) for the first nine months of the year earlier today drew a mixed reaction from telecomunications analysts and brokers on Wednesday.

Indosat reported net income of 361.6 billion rupiah, compared with 342.9 billion rupiah in the same nine-month period of 1995. It announced an earnings per shares (EPS) of 348.7 rupiah against 330.8 rupiah.
Indosat rose 25 rupiah to 7,325 on a turnover of 518,000 shares on the Jakarta stock market following the announcement.
Some analysts and brokers said the profit increase was slightly below expectations but they were generally happy with the result. Other analysts said the figures were within the anticipated range.
Agung Prabowo, analyst from major local brokerage firm Danareksa Sekuritas, said the results were in line with his expectations.
"With net profit growth of 6.8 percent for 1996, I believe Indosat can achieve my target of 490.4 billion rupiah by the end of the year," he said.

Another analyst from a domestic securities firm said he had changed his recommendation from "switch to Telkom" to "long-term buy" on expecations that contributions from Indosat associates would increase within the next year or two.

Some analysts from foreign securities houses said they were concerned over the company's third quarter cost figures. But they were quite happy with the call revenue and higher contributions from Indosat's associates.

David O'Neil of BZW Niaga Securities said the figures were slightly lower than expected. "I might revise down my target slightly, but before that I have check the cost structure for the fourth quarter," he said.
O'Neil said his 1996 net forecast was 490 billion rupiah and 570 billion rupiah for 1997.
But he added he was happy with the call revenue and contribution from cellular operator Telkomsel to the company.

Indosat President and Chief Executive Officer Tjahjono Soerjodibroto said the company estimated by year-end it would achieve a 13 to 15 percent growth in revenue and a 12 to 14 percent rise in operating income for 1996.
Indosat's international telephone traffic increased by 17.6 percent to 426.6 million minutes in the nine months to September 30, 1996, up from 362.8 million minutes in the same period last year.
